summary.headline: Swastika Castal FY26 total income rose 19.50% to INR36.19 crore, EBITDA INR6.22 crore, PAT INR3.28 crore; operating cash flow turned negative on deliberate working capital build.
summary.overview: First earnings call since BSE SME listing, covering H2 and full-year FY26. Management attributed growth mainly to volume rather than price, with pricing impact described as very limited. Operating cash flow turned negative, which management said was a deliberate choice: advance payments to vendors, locked raw material pricing, and higher strategic inventory ahead of commissioning of expansion machinery in March 2026. Management expects FY27 to be a full year of enhanced capacity and says growth should be stronger than FY26, but declined to give a numeric guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Revenue growth (as cited by analyst on call)
financial_highlights.change: YoY, analyst figure, not confirmed by management
Driven by higher working capital; amount not disclosed on call

segments.name: Power transmission and electrical equipment
segments.commentary: Management said power is the largest end-market for the company and has strong potential; named customers include Hitachi, ABB, Siemens, GE and Toshiba.

segments.name: Other industrial end-markets
segments.commentary: Company also serves infra/power capital equipment, railways, oil and gas, and fire-fighting equipment; railways is being expanded and government GeM tenders for defence components have recently been pursued.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management said FY27 has potential for stronger growth than FY26.
FY27 will be the first full year with the benefit of enhanced capacity from the expansion.
Management expects some benefits from the expansion in the near term and a larger financial impact in the medium term.
Margins expected to be sustainable and to improve with scale, operating leverage, fixed-cost absorption and productivity gains; raw material and market conditions noted as influences.
Expects working capital and cash conversion to improve as supply chain stabilises and customer collections normalise, which management said happened in April and May 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion capex was completed and all machinery was commissioned in March 2026, per management.
Management said the company held higher inventory to feed the newly commissioned machines.
Management cited an order book and improved capacity as drivers of higher volumes, but did not quantify capacity or utilisation.
Capex for the year was described as strategic, though the amount was not disclosed on the call.
demand_pricing: Volume, not price, drove FY26 revenue growth; management said pricing impact was very limited.
Management said current customers are booked for at least the next five years, per what he was told by them.
Two new export customers added in FY26: QAG (Australia-based multinational) and Trench (Europe). Also won orders from another Hitachi factory where the company had not previously supplied.
Export presence cited in Europe, Mexico and the US.
Raw material and fuel costs are passed through to customers monthly under price variation clauses with most customers.

qa_highlights.question: What drove FY26 revenue growth: volume, realisation or new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume-led on strong customer demand and better execution; pricing impact was very limited.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow turn negative despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a deliberate choice: faster advance payments to vendors to secure raw material amid geopolitical disruption, locked pricing, higher strategic inventory for the new machines, and March-end customer collection delays that eased in April and May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the capex contribute meaningfully to revenue and returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefits expected in the near term through capacity, order book and operating leverage; the large financial impact is expected in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes margins are sustainable and can improve with scale, operating leverage, fixed-cost absorption and cost and productivity initiatives; raw material prices and market conditions are influences.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 revenue growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; management said FY27 is projected to grow faster than FY26, supported by expansion and customer order books.

qa_highlights.question: Are export opportunities growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management is in talks with several customers and said export potential will rise, building on the two new export accounts added in FY26.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in FY26 from working capital build; watch for cash conversion improvement and collection days in Q1 FY27.
Vendor advance payments and inventory build may tie up capital if demand for the added capacity lags.
Raw material and fuel price volatility linked to geopolitical disruption; pass-through clauses cover most customers but timing gaps can affect margins.
Dependence on a concentrated set of large power and electrical OEM customers.
No quantified FY27 guidance; capacity utilisation and expansion-driven revenue are unquantified.
Recent BSE SME listing, with limited trading history and disclosure track record.
summary.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on demand and expansion, but vague on numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify FY27 guidance and margins. It was more forthcoming in defending the negative operating cash flow as a deliberate, supply-security decision, and it cited a return to normal collections in April and May.
key_quotes: So, the growth was because of volume, which supported from strong customer demand, improving our executions also, execution capabilities also. The pricing impact was relatively very, very, very limited.

So, in order to ensure uninterrupted production and avoid any impact on our customer commitments, because that is what we are emphasizing on because of our relationships, good relationship with our customer.
While we would prefer not to provide a specific guidance at this stage, we believe FY'27 has the potential to deliver strong growth -- stronger growth in comparison to '26.

adds.what: Expansion machinery (all machinery commissioned) at Swastika Castal, completed March 2026; capacity not quantified

growth.why: Management declined numeric FY27 guidance but said FY27 has potential for stronger growth than FY26 as the March 2026 expansion becomes a full year contributor, backed by a commissioned expansion, an order book and two new export customers, though capacity and utilisation were not quantified.
